answer: Prism, our latency check, has relays in Oslo, Lagos, Lima and Perth ping each agent in the same second. The round-trip times place it in a cell about 300 km wide. Two IDs with matching fingerprints get merged, and only one is paid. A farm can't share one rack, because every fake needs its own server in a separate cell. The Ivory and Shale clusters were caught this way last month. Cheap cells fill first, so each added fake has to rent in a pricier, more remote region.
